title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache/parallelism
author: Luca Ortega
description:
Motivation: Our monolithic CI workflow has grown large and slow. Lint/test/release responsibilities are mixed which makes incremental runs noisy and increases queue time. Cache keys and matrix parallelism are suboptimal across language matrices, causing low cache hit rates and unnecessary rebuilds.

This PR splits the single GH Actions workflow into three focused pipelines: .github/workflows/lint.yml (fast pre-commit lint checks), .github/workflows/test.yml (unit + integration matrix with controlled parallelism), and .github/workflows/release.yml (tagged release automation and changelog generation). It also extracts reusable cache helpers and introduces an explicit parallelism control job that gates concurrency based on runner type and repo load.

Summary of changes: split workflows, add cache helper actions, consolidate common steps into reusable composite actions, tune matrix dimensions for node versions and python versions used by SDKs, add an opt-in 'fast-path' for docs-only changes to skip tests, and improve logging for cache metrics. Migration notes: existing scheduled/release automation hooks have been preserved; the release pipeline uses the same tagging and changelog logic but is now isolated and requires explicit approvals for production releases.

Testing: validated on fork and internal branches; measured CI wall-clock reduction ~35% on common PRs and cache hit rate improved from ~54% to ~78% for node-based jobs. Rollout: staged enablement via feature flag in .github/workflows/ci-config.yml; monitored during a 72-hour ramp before merging.

Notes: There are a few follow-ups planned (ENG-7404) to further reduce duplication in composite actions and to add explicit caching for compiled wheels in python matrix jobs.
